title: Decision Framing Laboratory
scopeNote: This keeps the four decisions made one at a time with the equivalence withheld, and the side-by-side reframing afterwards. The manipulation of how certain the certain option is, the shift of the reference point itself, and the scenarios outside the stock-loss setting stay in the longer version.
summary: Four decisions about resources at risk, made one at a time with nothing explained. Two pairs of them turn out to contain identical numbers, described once in terms of what is saved and once in terms of what is lost.
learningObjectives: Recognise that two descriptions of identical outcomes can produce opposite choices.
Identify the reference point a description sets up, and how it moves.
State the usual direction of the effect: risk aversion for gains and risk seeking for losses.
Explain why withholding the equivalence is necessary for the demonstration to work.
Recognise that consistency is not superior reasoning and that switching is not a simple error.
interactionTypes: four decisions presented one at a time with the equivalence withheld
the certain option alternating position so answering by position is visible
a paired reveal setting the two framings of each problem side by side
feedback that names the learner's own two choices and whether they switched
wording that handles consistency, the usual direction and the unusual one differently
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. Every choice is held in the browser and is gone when the page is closed.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout, with every option a labelled button. Nothing is timed and there is no motion. The reveal is built from real elements rather than from markup strings, and each card carries a state that distinguishes a switched pair from an unswitched one by a hidden note as well as by colour. The two framings of a problem are set out as full text in both cards, so the comparison does not depend on remembering what was asked earlier. The emptied options fieldset is hidden at the reveal rather than left drawing an empty box.
dataStatus: Invented scenarios about vaccine crates and woodland. No real event, organisation or figure is described, and nothing is a norm.
simulationNotes: Two problems, each asked once in a gain frame and once in a loss frame, interleaved so that the two halves of a pair are never adjacent and the two problems use different goods. Within a pair the numbers are identical: saving 200 of 600 is losing 400 of 600, and a one-in-three chance of saving all is a two-in-three chance of losing all. Withholding the equivalence is not decoration; a learner told in advance what is being examined will answer the second version to match the first and the demonstration is gone. The certain option alternates position across the four decisions, so a learner answering by position produces a visibly inconsistent pattern rather than a spuriously clean one. All three outcome patterns are given their own wording, including full consistency, which is treated as a reasonable place to end up rather than as a failure.
readmeTopic: how the same outcomes described two ways produce opposite choices
